title: Indie
tagline: Independent spirit, close-up detail, open doors.
summary: Indie describes music shaped by independent scenes, labels and aesthetics rather than one fixed sound. Guitar pop, folk, electronic experiments and lo-fi recordings all meet under the name. The umbrella is wide and its meaning has shifted as independent sounds entered the mainstream. Here, indie is a listening path through self-directed communities, distinctive songwriting and artists who made room for alternatives to dominant pop and rock conventions.

history.heading: Independent networks
history.text: Punk encouraged musicians to form bands, make records and organize shows without waiting for major institutions. Small labels, fanzines and local venues connected audiences across cities. Independence was both a practical route to release music and an attitude that valued personal expression over polish.

history.heading: A wider guitar language
history.text: College radio, UK independent labels and underground clubs supported jangling guitars, noisy textures and melodic songwriting. Scenes remained distinct, but touring and mail-order records created links between them. The category described how music circulated as much as how it sounded, leaving space for experimentation.

history.heading: Alternative becomes visible
history.text: Some independent guitar music found large audiences, bringing underground sounds into mainstream media. Shoegaze, Britpop and lo-fi songwriting each developed different responses to fame and production. The decade made indie more recognizable while prompting artists to keep building smaller, self-defined communities.

history.heading: A many-sided home
history.text: Digital distribution and online communities made independent releases easier to discover across borders. Indie came to include electronic pop, folk, bedroom recordings and hybrid scenes, sometimes as a sound and sometimes as a production identity. Spanish and Catalan scenes added local voices to this international exchange.

pillars.name: The Velvet Underground
pillars.why: Their adventurous arrangements and downtown sensibility became a reference point for artists working outside conventional pop formulas.

pillars.name: Sonic Youth
pillars.why: The band brought experimental guitar tunings and underground practice into a durable independent career, influencing alternative scenes internationally.

pillars.name: Pixies
pillars.why: Their quiet-loud dynamics and compact, surprising songs became a widely heard template for independent guitar bands.
